description: graph-projector (docs/01 §2 service 14, docs/03): a Kafka consumer service that consumes txn.lifecycle + agent.verdicts + decision.log, projects into Neo4j (entities + relationships per docs/03 §3) and Postgres read models (docs/03 §4), with idempotent upserts keyed by event_id/transaction_id (docs/01 §6). It OWNS runtime read-model population and calls acip_common.bootstrap.ensure_read_model_schema on startup (this is the always-on side of fix A.1). Health edge + structured logging + trace_id. Depends on FEAT-001 (bootstrap helper). Independent of FEAT-002 (agents) at the code level but ordered after it so the full agent->verdict->decision->projection chain can be verified together; the projector consumes events any producer emits, so it does not import agent code. Follows the standard skeleton (non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile, uv workspace member, FastAPI /healthz+/readyz, Settings config).
steps: services/graph-projector/{Dockerfile,pyproject.toml,src/graph_projector/{__init__,main,consumer,neo4j_projector,postgres_projector}.py,tests/test_projector.py}. consumer.py: one acip_common.kafka.EventConsumer subscribed to [TXN_LIFECYCLE, AGENT_VERDICTS, DECISION_LOG] with group.id 'graph-projector', streaming EventEnvelopes and dispatching by event_type to the two projectors, committing AFTER a successful project (at-least-once; idempotent upserts dedupe replays, docs/01 §6). bind_trace_id from the envelope trace_id.

postgres_projector.py: on startup call acip_common.bootstrap.ensure_read_model_schema(settings.postgres_dsn) (fix A.1). For every envelope write an event_journal row INSERT (event_id, transaction_id, event_type, occurred_at) ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING (idempotent by event_id). For TXN_CREATED (TxnCreatedPayload): upsert transactions(id, customer_id, amount, status='CREATED', decision=NULL) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE. For DECISION_RENDERED (DecisionRenderedPayload): upsert decisions(transaction_id, decision, composite_score, strategy) ON CONFLICT (transaction_id) DO UPDATE, and update transactions.decision/status. For AGENT_VERDICT_PRODUCED (AgentVerdictProducedPayload): upsert agent_verdicts(transaction_id, agent, score, decision_hint) ON CONFLICT (transaction_id, agent) DO UPDATE. For TXN_EXECUTED/DECLINED/CHALLENGED (TxnTerminalPayload): update transactions.status/decision. Columns match scripts/seed.py exactly. Best-effort per event: a DB error logs + is sent to handling (log) without crashing the loop.

neo4j_projector.py: idempotent MERGE upserts per docs/03 §3. For TXN_CREATED: MERGE (c:Customer {id}), MERGE (t:Transaction {id}) SET amount/currency/status/method_type, MERGE (c)-[:PLACED]->(t); if a device fingerprint is present in the payload context MERGE (d:Device {id}) MERGE (t)-[:FROM_DEVICE]->(d) and MERGE (d)-[:LINKED_TO]->(c). For DECISION_RENDERED: MERGE (de:DecisionEvent {id: event_id}) SET decision/score/at, MERGE (t)-[:HAS_DECISION]->(de); if a chosen route is present MERGE (p:Processor {id: route}) MERGE (t)-[:ROUTED_TO]->(p). Node/edge keys use ids so replays are idempotent. Driver opens lazily and is degradation-tolerant (log + skip on connect/read failure) so a Neo4j outage does not crash the projector.

main.py: FastAPI app with GET /healthz ({status:ok}) and GET /readyz (ready once the consumer thread is live); lifespan starts the consumer loop in a daemon thread (same pattern as the agents' health app) and calls ensure_read_model_schema once at startup. Non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile copying pyproject.toml+uv.lock+libs/acip-common+services/graph-projector, `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --package graph-projector`, uid 10001, EXPOSE 8000, CMD uvicorn graph_projector.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000. Deps: acip-common, fastapi==0.115.6, uvicorn[standard]==0.34.0, neo4j==5.27.0, psycopg[binary]==3.2.3.

Workspace wiring: REMOVE services/graph-projector from root pyproject.toml [tool.uv.workspace].exclude, add graph-projector = { workspace = true } to [tool.uv.sources] AND to [dependency-groups].dev; uv sync.

tests/test_projector.py: with Kafka/Neo4j/Postgres mocked, assert (a) each event_type routes to the correct projector method (TXN_CREATED->transactions+Customer/Transaction; AGENT_VERDICT_PRODUCED->agent_verdicts; DECISION_RENDERED->decisions+DecisionEvent; terminal->status update; every event->event_journal), (b) upserts are idempotent (applying the same envelope twice issues ON CONFLICT upserts / MERGE and yields one row/one node - assert the SQL/Cypher used ON CONFLICT/MERGE and the fake store ends with a single entry), (c) the consumer commits AFTER projecting, (d) a store outage is swallowed (logged) and the loop continues.
acceptance_criteria: graph-projector consumes txn.lifecycle + agent.verdicts + decision.log on one consumer (group 'graph-projector') and projects each event to Neo4j and Postgres, committing AFTER a successful project.
On startup it calls acip_common.bootstrap.ensure_read_model_schema so read models exist on a fresh stack with no seed (fix A.1 always-on owner).

Projections are idempotent: Postgres writes use ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE/NOTHING keyed by primary key / event_id and Neo4j uses MERGE keyed by id, so replaying an event produces no duplicates; a test proves it.
Postgres table shapes written match scripts/seed.py exactly; Neo4j nodes/edges match docs/03 §3.
graph-projector is a uv workspace member with a non-root python:3.11-slim Dockerfile and FastAPI GET /healthz + /readyz; a store outage degrades (logs) without crashing the consumer loop.
verification: uv run pytest services/graph-projector  (all pass, incl. routing + idempotency + commit-after-project tests)
uv run mypy libs services  (clean, strict)

MODULES:
- consumer.ProjectorConsumer(settings_kafka_bootstrap, postgres_projector, neo4j_projector, *, consumer=None). One acip_common.kafka.EventConsumer, group CONSUMER_GROUP='graph-projector', SOURCE_TOPICS=[TXN_LIFECYCLE, AGENT_VERDICTS, DECISION_LOG]. consume_forever(poll_timeout=1.0): per envelope bind_trace_id, project to Postgres THEN Neo4j, then commit AFTER the project (docs/01 §6). .running property drives /readyz; .postgres property exposes the schema owner for the lifespan bootstrap; .close() closes consumer + neo4j driver. Projectors swallow their own store errors so a store outage degrades without crashing the loop.
- postgres_projector.PostgresProjector(postgres_dsn). ensure_schema() -> acip_common.bootstrap.ensure_read_model_schema (fix A.1 always-on owner). project(envelope): lazy psycopg import; one connection/txn; _journal() writes event_journal (event_id,transaction_id,event_type,occurred_at) ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING for EVERY event; _apply dispatch: TXN_CREATED->transactions upsert (status 'CREATED', decision NULL) ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE; DECISION_RENDERED->decisions upsert ON CONFLICT (transaction_id) DO UPDATE + UPDATE transactions decision/status; AGENT_VERDICT_PRODUCED->agent_verdicts upsert ON CONFLICT (transaction_id, agent) DO UPDATE; TXN_EXECUTED/DECLINED/CHALLENGED->UPDATE transactions status/decision. Columns match scripts/seed.py exactly. Best-effort: DB error logged + swallowed. Decision->status map mirrors commerce_orchestrator.persistence.status_for_decision.
- neo4j_projector.Neo4jProjector(neo4j_uri, neo4j_auth). Lazy driver (GraphDatabase.driver; _ensure_driver logs + returns None on connect failure). project(envelope): TXN_CREATED -> MERGE (c:Customer{id}) MERGE (t:Transaction{id}) SET amount/currency/status/method_type MERGE (c)-[:PLACED]->(t); if context.device_fingerprint present MERGE (d:Device{id}) MERGE (t)-[:FROM_DEVICE]->(d) MERGE (d)-[:LINKED_TO]->(c). DECISION_RENDERED -> MERGE (de:DecisionEvent{id:event_id}) SET decision/score/at MERGE (t)-[:HAS_DECISION]->(de); if payload.route present MERGE (p:Processor{id:route}) MERGE (t)-[:ROUTED_TO]->(p). All keys are ids so MERGE is idempotent on replay. Non-graph events (verdict/terminal) are a no-op. Session error logged + skipped (degradation-tolerant). _parse_neo4j_auth matches scripts/seed.py. close() closes the driver.
- main.py: FastAPI(title graph-projector) with GET /healthz ({status:ok}) and GET /readyz (503 until _consumer.running). Module-level _consumer built from Settings. Lifespan calls _consumer.postgres.ensure_schema() (fix A.1 at startup) then starts _consumer.consume_forever in a daemon thread 'graph-projector-consume' (same pattern as the agent health app) and closes the consumer on shutdown.

TESTS (tests/test_projector.py, 10, Kafka/Neo4j/Postgres mocked): routing per event_type + journaling; postgres idempotent on replay (one agent_verdicts row + one journal row); neo4j created MERGEs Customer/Transaction/Device + PLACED/FROM_DEVICE/LINKED_TO; created-without-device skips Device; decision MERGEs DecisionEvent + Processor route; neo4j idempotent on replay (one node per id); non-graph event no-op; SOURCE_TOPICS == three source topics; commit-after-project order ['project','commit']; store outage (both Postgres connect + Neo4j session raising) swallowed and both events still committed. Test module uniquely named test_projector.py, no tests/__init__.py (matches service convention).

NOTE: payload shapes read via model_validate -> TxnCreatedPayload (customer_id, amount, currency, payment_method.type, context.device_fingerprint), DecisionRenderedPayload (decision, composite_score, strategy, route), AgentVerdictProducedPayload (agent, verdict.score, verdict.decision_hint), TxnTerminalPayload (decision). neo4j ships type info so no mypy override needed. Did not touch docs/ or any Phase 1/2/FEAT-002 files beyond the root pyproject workspace wiring.
